walks.name: SF State
walks.vibe: A big commuter campus with a busy plaza and a mall next door.

start.n: Take the M Ocean View to the SF State stop.
start.a: 19th Ave and Holloway Ave, San Francisco, CA

stops.t: AS Information Center, Cesar Chavez Student Center
stops.n: Bring flyers to the Plaza Level desk for a stamp. Staff post them on the general boards for you.
Flyers go only on the blue cloth boards in the elevator lobbies and near room 83 on the ground floor. Ask at the desk first.
Heytea, Wanpo Tea, Matcha Cafe Maiko and 85C are here. Ask each counter if a flyer or small card can go out.
SF library boards go through the library's information office first. Ask staff how to submit.
A student favorite one stop up the M line. Grab a donut and ask about their counter.
stops.a: 163 West Portal Ave, San Francisco, CA

walks.rule: Flyers in the Cesar Chavez Student Center are approved, stamped and posted by the AS Information Center on the Plaza Level. They stay up about two weeks. Nothing on columns, windows or railings.

walks.name: City College, Ocean Campus
walks.vibe: A friendly community college with an open plaza and Ocean Ave cafes.

start.n: Walk up Frida Kahlo Way from the station.
start.a: 401 Geneva Ave, San Francisco, CA

stops.n: Sign in and pick up the posting rules. Ask which boards have room today.
stops.a: 50 Frida Kahlo Way, San Francisco, CA

stops.n: Between Smith Hall and the Student Union. After signing in you can hand out flyers here.
stops.a: 50 Frida Kahlo Way, San Francisco, CA

stops.n: A camping-themed cafe on Ocean Ave. Ask about their counter or board.
Busy with students all day. Ask the staff before leaving anything.
SF library boards go through the library's information office first. Ask staff how to submit.

walks.rule: Outside groups sign in first at the Student Activities Office, Student Union room 205. It is a notice, not an approval. Post only on posting boards, up to 11x17, tacks only, one per board, 20 flyers at most.

walks.name: Late-night study cafes
walks.vibe: Where students and young builders work after dark.

start.n: Take BART or Muni Metro to Montgomery.
start.a: Market St and Montgomery St, San Francisco, CA

stops.n: The 24/7 cafe run by the startup Corgi, on a small lane off Kearny. Mostly founders and young tech workers. Last seen open in late September, so check first.
A Yemeni coffee house open until 8 pm daily. Ask about their counter.
Yemeni coffee and pastries, open until about 10 pm, near Academy of Art buildings.
stops.a: 199 New Montgomery St, San Francisco, CA

stops.n: Another late-night Yemeni cafe in SoMa. Ask the staff first.
Open daily until 11 pm and full of laptops. Ask about a flyer spot.

walks.rule: No campus rules here. Ask staff at each cafe before leaving a flyer, and take it back if they say no.

walks.name: USF
walks.vibe: A hilltop campus ringed by Haight and NoPa coffee shops.

start.n: Take the 5 Fulton or 43 Masonic.
start.a: Fulton St and Masonic Ave, San Francisco, CA

stops.n: A laptop-friendly roastery by the park. Ask about their board.
A calm neighborhood cafe close to campus. Ask the barista first.
A small Divisadero cafe students recommend. Ask about window space.
A big bright room with lots of seating. Treat yourself and ask about posting.

walks.rule: USF posts only flyers from its own clubs and departments for campus events. Outside groups can't post, so focus on the cafes. A USF student club could co-host.

walks.name: UCSF Parnassus and Inner Sunset
walks.vibe: Health science students spilling down the hill to 9th Avenue.

start.n: Take the N Judah to 9th and Irving.
start.a: 9th Ave and Irving St, San Francisco, CA

stops.n: A worker-owned bakery, open Tuesday to Sunday. Ask the counter about flyers.
Japanese sando and matcha. A nice treat between stops.
Right at the park end of 9th Ave. Take a breather.

walks.rule: UCSF boards are only for UCSF people and registered campus groups. Outside groups need an invitation from a campus organization, so stick to the 9th Ave shops.

walks.name: Academy of Art, downtown
walks.vibe: Art students between New Montgomery classrooms and Sutter Street dorms.

start.n: Walk down New Montgomery from the station.
start.a: Market St and New Montgomery St, San Francisco, CA

stops.n: Ask whether an outside wellness event can be listed. Nothing in the dorms on Sutter and Pine.
stops.a: 79 New Montgomery St, San Francisco, CA

stops.n: Right on New Montgomery and open late. Ask about their counter.
stops.a: 199 New Montgomery St, San Francisco, CA

stops.n: A free coworking-style cafe on Post, open weekdays. Ask staff about community postings.
A study-friendly cafe near the Pine St dorms. Ask the staff first.

walks.rule: Board notices need university approval and the dorms ban outside flyers. Ask Campus Life, then stick to nearby cafes.

walks.name: UCSF Mission Bay
walks.vibe: A new waterfront campus with a handful of good cafes.

start.n: Take the T Third.
start.a: 3rd St and 16th St, San Francisco, CA

stops.n: A roomy cafe near campus, open daily. Ask about their board.
stops.a: 610 Long Bridge St, San Francisco, CA

stops.n: Opened August 2026 on Mission Creek. Ask the new owners about a spot.
SF library boards go through the library's information office first. Ask staff how.
A Yemeni coffee house open late. A good place to end.

walks.rule: Same UCSF rules as Parnassus: campus boards are for UCSF people only. Stick to the cafes and the library.

walks.name: UC Law SF and Civic Center
walks.vibe: Law students around Civic Center and the Main Library.

start.n: Take BART or Muni Metro to Civic Center.
start.a: Market St and 8th St, San Francisco, CA

stops.n: Ask at student services whether outside events can be posted. Nothing up without a yes.
Boards are cleared by the library's information office. They take cultural and educational items, not commercial ones.
A steady student and city-worker crowd. Ask the staff first.
stops.a: 399 Golden Gate Ave, San Francisco, CA

walks.rule: No public posting policy was found for UC Law SF. Ask student services before posting anything on campus.

walks.name: Sproul Plaza
walks.vibe: The busiest student crossing at Cal. Smile, offer, move on.

start.n: About 12 minutes from Downtown Berkeley BART along Bancroft.
start.a: Bancroft Way and Telegraph Ave, Berkeley, CA

stops.n: Stand out of the walkway and offer half-sheets to people who slow down. Keep off the fire lane in front of the Savio Steps.
The coffee line is long between classes. Offer flyers to people waiting outside, not inside.
stops.a: Golden Bear Cafe, Sproul Plaza, Berkeley, CA

stops.n: A natural funnel. Stand to one side so people can pass.
Ask the info desk which boards are open to the public. Inside, flyers only go on approved boards.
Also a public expression area. Catch students heading to the food court.

walks.rule: Anyone may hand out non-commercial flyers outdoors. Upper and Lower Sproul are open 6 am to midnight with no booking. Non-members can't set up a table, chair or display.

walks.name: Durant food court
walks.vibe: Late-night food, boba lines and students everywhere after dark.

start.n: Two blocks south of Sproul Plaza.
start.a: Durant Ave and Telegraph Ave, Berkeley, CA

stops.n: A classic study-break stop. Ask staff before leaving flyers.
Voted best coffee shop in 2025. Ask if there is a board or counter spot.
A cluster of small restaurants. Offer flyers to people waiting for takeout.
Boba and snacks, open very late. Good for evening handouts.
Voted best late-night food in 2025. Chat with the line, then ask staff about leaving a few.

walks.rule: City sidewalk and private shops. Ask each shop before leaving anything, and keep the sidewalk clear.

walks.name: Telegraph Avenue
walks.vibe: Old bookshops, records and boba, one block from campus.

start.n: About 12 minutes from Downtown Berkeley BART.
start.a: Telegraph Ave and Bancroft Way, Berkeley, CA

stops.n: Voted best boba in Berkeley in 2025. Chat with people in line and ask staff if you can leave a few.
Open Wednesday to Sunday, 11 to 7. Ask at the counter about community flyers.
A Telegraph landmark. Ask the front desk politely if they take event flyers.
A laid-back study cafe a few blocks south. Ask about a board or counter space.

walks.rule: City sidewalk and private shops, not campus. Always ask staff first, and never tape to poles or walls.

walks.name: Moffitt and Memorial Glade
walks.vibe: The study crowd around a newly reopened library.

start.n: From Sather Gate, walk north past Dwinelle, about 5 minutes.
start.a: Memorial Glade, Berkeley, CA

stops.n: Students sit and take breaks here. Walk the paths and offer a flyer with a short hello.
At Moffitt's entrance, reopened in 2026. Stand outside and catch people coming for coffee.
Heavy crossings on the hour. Hand out between class changes.
Only boards designated public, up to 11x14 inches. The Student Union info desk has the list.

walks.rule: Hand out flyers outdoors only. Moffitt needs a Cal ID, and inside buildings you may post only on boards marked public.

walks.name: Downtown study cafes
walks.vibe: Study cafes along Shattuck, from the library to North Shattuck.

start.n: Get off at Downtown Berkeley.
start.a: Shattuck Ave and Center St, Berkeley, CA

stops.n: Hand a flyer to staff and ask for the community board.
Popular with students at the west edge of campus. Ask about a board.
Lots of outlets and studiers. Ask kindly.
A board game cafe open late, full of students in the evening. Ask about community flyers.

walks.rule: City sidewalk and private shops, so ask first. Library staff post nonprofit notices for up to 30 days.

walks.name: Units and Channing
walks.vibe: Freshman country: mealtime sidewalks and cafes near the halls.

start.n: Three blocks south of Sproul Plaza.
start.a: 2650 Durant Ave, Berkeley, CA

stops.n: Students head to the dining hall at lunch and dinner. Offer flyers from the public sidewalk.
Same idea on Haste St. Keep it light and don't follow anyone to the door.
A nonprofit cafe that trains refugee baristas. Ask kindly about a board.
A huge patio full of students, open late. Ask staff first, then chat outside.

walks.rule: No posting or handing out inside or around residence halls without approval. Stay on the public sidewalk and never enter lobbies or courtyards.

walks.name: Euclid and North Gate
walks.vibe: Engineering and science crowd, small cafes, quieter streets.

start.n: About 15 minutes up Hearst from Downtown Berkeley BART.
start.a: Hearst Ave and Euclid Ave, Berkeley, CA

stops.n: A steady flow toward the engineering halls. Offer flyers on the sidewalk.
stops.a: Hearst Ave and Euclid Ave, Berkeley, CA

stops.n: A student favorite with lots of outlets. Ask about leaving a few.
A Northside classic. Ask the counter about a community board.
A small busy cafe by the engineering halls with picnic tables. Offer flyers to people outside.

walks.rule: Euclid is city sidewalk and private shops, so ask first. Across Hearst is campus: handing out is fine, posting is boards only.

walks.name: Piedmont Ave and I-House
walks.vibe: Grad and international students, Greek Row and a hillside dorm.

start.n: 10 minutes on foot from Sproul.
start.a: 2300 College Ave, Berkeley, CA

stops.n: A walk-in cafe inside I-House. Ask the front desk if there is a community board.
Wide sidewalks along Greek Row. Offer flyers to passersby only, nothing on houses or cars.
stops.a: Piedmont Ave and Bancroft Way, Berkeley, CA

stops.n: Offer flyers on the sidewalk near the dining commons at mealtimes.

walks.rule: Fraternity and sorority houses are private: never post on them or walk in. Clark Kerr is a residence hall, so stay on the sidewalk.

walks.name: College Ave to Elmwood
walks.vibe: A calm stroll south where grad students live and study.

start.n: Buses run along College Ave.
start.a: College Ave and Bancroft Way, Berkeley, CA

stops.n: Popular with students. Ask about a board.
Open daily with outdoor seating. Ask staff before leaving flyers.
Hand a flyer to staff and ask for the community board.

walks.rule: All city sidewalk and shops. Ask staff first. The library branch posts nonprofit notices through staff.

walks.name: Laney College
walks.vibe: A lakeside campus near Chinatown boba and the Main Library.

start.n: Laney is one block east of the station.
start.a: Lake Merritt BART, Oakland, CA

stops.n: Get your approval first, then post only in the marked spots. Not on doors, windows, posts or trees.
A Chinatown boba spot. Ask if they have a board.
A loose-leaf tea house in Chinatown. Closed Mondays.
Hand a dated copy to staff for approval. Items stay up to 30 days.
Across the street from Laney. Rest in the gardens.

walks.rule: Outside groups can apply. Student Services approves all flyers through the Laney approvals page, 24 to 48 hours. Up to 12x18, 20 postings, two weeks or until the day after the event.

walks.name: Mills at Northeastern
walks.vibe: A quiet wooded campus beside the Laurel District shops.

start.n: AC Transit runs along MacArthur Blvd.
start.a: 5000 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland, CA

stops.n: The campus hangout. Ask staff who approves postings.
Roasts on site. Ask about their community board.
A pastry stop next door. Ask about counter space.

walks.rule: No public posting policy was found. Ask student life on campus before posting, or stick to the Laurel shops.

walks.name: Stanford and Palo Alto
walks.vibe: Open kiosks at White Plaza, then cafes along University Ave.

start.n: The free Marguerite shuttle runs to campus.
start.a: 95 University Ave, Palo Alto, CA

stops.n: Post on the public kiosks next to Tresidder Union, then hand out in the plaza.
The original Coupa, a long-time Stanford hangout. Ask about their board.
A popular study spot. Ask the staff first.
Opens early and fills with students. Grab a cup and ask.

walks.rule: Anyone may post at the public kiosks in White Plaza and around campus, and visitors may hand out leaflets in White Plaza. No tables for visitors, and dorm boards are for Stanford only.

walks.name: San Jose State
walks.vibe: A downtown campus with a shared city library and boba on every block.

start.n: VTA light rail, Blue or Green line.
start.a: S 2nd St and Paseo de San Antonio, San Jose, CA

stops.n: Ask at the info desk how an outside group can get flyers on the general boards.
Ground floor of the shared city and university library. A real student hub.
stops.a: 150 E San Fernando St, San Jose, CA

stops.n: Won the student paper's boba ranking. Ask about their counter.
stops.a: 110 E San Fernando St, San Jose, CA

stops.n: The original downtown cafe. Ask about a spot for a flyer.

walks.rule: Outside groups must contact Student Involvement or Event Services before any activity on campus. General boards allow one poster per group, up to 11x17, tacks or staples.

walks.name: Cal State East Bay
walks.vibe: A hilltop campus above a small, friendly downtown on B Street.

start.n: Downtown is steps away. Campus is a bus or shuttle up the hill.
start.a: 699 B St, Hayward, CA

stops.n: Campus guidelines name students and staff as posters, so ask SLIC before posting anything here.
Steady student traffic near BART. Ask about the community board.
A sweet bakery stop on B Street. Ask about their counter.
The downtown library. Ask staff about the community board.

walks.rule: Student Life and Involvement (SLIC), room 2011 in the University Union, handles posting. General boards may be open to the public, so stop by SLIC first to confirm.
